verses.text: This is the message the LORD spoke through Jeremiah the prophet about Babylon and the land of the Babylonians.

"Announce it among the nations and proclaim it. Raise a flag and proclaim it. Do not hide anything. Say, 'Babylon has been captured! Bel is put to shame. Marduk is terrified. Her images are put to shame, and her idols are terrified.'
For a nation from the north will attack her and turn her land into a wasteland. No one will live in it. Both people and animals will run away.
In those days and at that time," says the LORD, "the people of Israel and the people of Judah will come together. They will come weeping as they look for the LORD their God.
They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will say, 'Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in a covenant that will last forever and never be forgotten.'
My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds led them astray and made them wander on the mountains. They roamed from mountain to hill and forgot their own resting place.
Everyone who found them devoured them. Their enemies said, 'We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, their true home of righteousness, the LORD, the hope of their ancestors.'
Run away from Babylon! Leave the land of the Babylonians! Be like the goats that lead the flock.

For look, I am stirring up a group of great nations from the land of the north to attack Babylon. They will line up for battle against her and capture her. Their arrows are like skilled warriors who never come back empty-handed.
Babylon will be robbed, and all who rob her will have plenty," says the LORD.
"You people of Babylon are glad and celebrate, you who robbed my people. You frolic like a young cow in the grain, and you neigh like strong horses.
But your mother city will be deeply ashamed. She who gave you birth will be disgraced. She will become the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, a desert.
Because of the LORD's anger, no one will live there. She will be completely deserted. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be shocked and will gasp at all her wounds.
Line up for battle all around Babylon, all you archers. Shoot at her! Do not hold back your arrows, because she has sinned against the LORD.
Shout the battle cry against her from every side! She surrenders. Her towers fall. Her walls are torn down. This is the LORD's revenge. Take revenge on her! Do to her what she has done to others.
Cut off from Babylon those who plant the seed and those who swing the sickle at harvest time. Because of the cruel sword, everyone will go back to their own people and run to their own land.
Israel is like scattered sheep chased by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured them. Last of all, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon crushed their bones."
So this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: "Look, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, just as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to its own pasture. They will graze on Carmel and Bashan. They will eat their fill on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

In those days and at that time," says the LORD, "people will search for Israel's guilt, but there will be none. They will look for Judah's sins, but none will be found, because I will forgive the survivors I leave behind.
Attack the land of Merathaim and the people living in Pekod. Kill them and completely destroy them," says the LORD. "Do everything I have commanded you.
The noise of battle fills the land, the noise of great destruction.
How broken and shattered is the hammer of the whole earth! How Babylon has become a ruin among the nations!
I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and captured, because you fought against the LORD.
The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his anger. For the Lord GOD of Armies has work to do in the land of the Babylonians.
Come against her from far away. Break open her storehouses. Pile her up like heaps of grain. Destroy her completely. Leave nothing of her.
Kill all her young bulls. Let them go down to the slaughter. How terrible for them! Their day has come, the time for them to be punished.
Listen to those who run away and escape from the land of Babylon. They come to announce in Zion how the LORD our God has taken revenge, revenge for his temple.

Call together the archers against Babylon, all who use the bow. Camp all around her. Let no one escape. Pay her back for what she has done. Do to her as she has done to others. For she was arrogant toward the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
So her young men will fall in her streets, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day," says the LORD.
"Look, I am against you, you proud one," says the Lord GOD of Armies. "Your day has come, the time for me to punish you.
The proud one will stumble and fall, and no one will help him up. I will set fire to his towns, and it will burn up everything around him."
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah too. All their captors hold them tightly and refuse to let them go.
But their Redeemer is strong. The LORD of Armies is his name. He will strongly defend their case so that he can bring rest to the earth and unrest to the people of Babylon.
A sword against the Babylonians!" says the LORD. "A sword against the people of Babylon, against her officials and her wise men!
A sword against her false prophets, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be terrified!
A sword against her horses and chariots, and against all the foreign soldiers among her, and they will become as weak as women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be looted!
A drought on her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of idols, and the people are crazy about their idols.
So desert creatures and hyenas will live there, and ostriches will live there too. No one will ever live there again. No one will settle there for all generations.
As when God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring towns," says the LORD, "no one will live there. No human being will stay there.
Look, an army is coming from the north. A great nation and many kings are being stirred up from the far ends of the earth.

They are armed with bows and spears. They are cruel and show no mercy. They sound like the roaring sea as they ride on their horses. They come lined up like soldiers for battle to attack you, daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard reports about them, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like a woman in labor.

Look, like a lion coming up from the thick bushes along the Jordan to a rich pasture, I will suddenly chase Babylon from its land. I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who can challenge me? What shepherd can stand against me?"

So listen to the plan the LORD has made against Babylon, and what he intends to do to the land of the Babylonians: Even the youngest of the flock will be dragged away. He will completely destroy their pasture.
At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth will shake. Its cry will be heard among the nations.
